events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Coffee, AL
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
At 1242 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 5 and 12 inches of rain have fallen. Additional
rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Heavy rain producing flash
flooding.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Elba, Enterprise, Fort Rucker, New Brockton, Lee, Woodland Grove
Church, Camp Humming Hills, Richburg, Wise Mill, Arcus, Mixons
Crossroads, Clintonville, Lowry Mill, Carl Folsom A/p, Tabernacle,
New Haven, Turner Crossroads, Victoria, Camp Alaflo Bsa and Jack.

Rain is in the process of tapering off. However, small streams,
creeks and rivers will rise quickly early this morning as runoff
makes its way downhill and downstream.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to one foot of inundation above ground level
possible in low lying areas due to tidal flooding.

* WHERE...Shoreline in Anne Arundel County.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon through Sunday evening,
especially around the time of high tide.

* IMPACTS...At 3.2 feet, water begins to approach businesses on
Dock Street in Annapolis. The City Dock parking lot is
flooded. Compromise Street is flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Tides one and a half to two feet above
normal. The next high tide at Annapolis U.S. Naval Academy is at
5:26 AM and 6:08 PM.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Conecuh County in south central Alabama...
Covington County in south central Alabama...
Southern Crenshaw County in south central Alabama...
Eastern Escambia County in south central Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 900 AM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Expect many
areas of slow moving or standing water. It will take several hours
for all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1238 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 4 and 8 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Andalusia, Opp, Brewton, Florala, East Brewton, Brantley, River
Falls, Red Level, Lockhart, Dozier, Heath, Gantt, Glenwood,
Riverview, Carolina, Beck, Stanley, Red Oak, Loango and Rhump.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central South Carolina, including the
following areas, Aiken, Bamberg, Barnwell, Central Orangeburg,
Northwestern Orangeburg and Southeastern Orangeburg.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT this morning through Sunday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Isaias continues to move inland overnight with a band of
associated heavy rainfall developing near the area Saturday.
While the exact location of where this banding will occur is
uncertain, higher rainfall totals potentially moving into eastern
GA and southern SC. Rainfall totals of 3-6" are possible within
this band of heavier rain Saturday morning into Saturday night.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Ashe; Alleghany; Surry; Watauga; Wilkes; Grayson; Carroll; Floyd; Patrick
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of North Carolina, including the following areas,
Alleghany NC, Ashe, Surry, Watauga and Wilkes and southwest
Virginia, including the following areas, Carroll, Floyd, Grayson
and Patrick.

* WHEN...From 11 AM EDT this morning through Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Low-water crossings
may be flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with
debris. Extensive street flooding and flooding of creeks and rivers
are possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Upslope rainfall from a rather strong southeasterly Low level jet
from the remnants of Isaias will bring increased precipitation
along the crest of the southern Blue Ridge from Floyd county
extending southwestward to Watauga county. Widespread rainfall
totals of 2-4 inches with locally higher totals in the 5-6 range
will be possible, especially for areas like Meadows of Dan,
Boone, and Blowing Rock. These higher totals may lead to isolated
instances of landslides along slopes that have been modified by
humans like embankments or cut slopes. These areas may also see
increased rises on local streamflows that may lead to flooding
across low-water crossings.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Ashe; Watauga; Tazewell; Smyth; Grayson; Mercer; Summers; Western Greenbrier
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...East winds 15 to 25 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...In North Carolina, Ashe and Watauga Counties. In Virginia,
Grayson, Smyth, and Tazewell Counties. In West Virginia, Mercer,
Summers, and Western Greenbrier Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to 11 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Strong easterly to southeasterly winds from
the remnants of Isaias will move over the region today into Sunday,
which may lead to downed trees and power poles and subsequently
power outages across higher terrain locations from NW North
Carolina to SE West Virginia.
